title: Plugin metadata
description: JSON Schema for plugin.json — IDE autocompletion + JSON validation

$schema.description: JSON Schema reference — used for IDE autocompletion
$schema.$comment: $schema is used only for IDE autocompletion; no JSON Schema validation is performed at runtime

pluginId.description: 🔴 Plugin identity — immutable once published (mirrors VS Code's publisher.name). Everything keys off it: install directory {userData}/plugins/<pluginId>/, distribution file name <pluginId>.linkdesk-plugin, marketplace dedup key, uninstall tombstone key, and update reconciliation. Strongly recommended to declare it explicitly: when omitted it falls back to the project directory name, but repository names and local directory names are free-form — rename the directory and the identity changes with it, and none of the five consequences (two install directories side by side / tombstone mismatch / duplicate marketplace entries / silently broken update chain / plugin data appearing lost) reports an error. Character set: letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`; the first character must be a letter or a digit. It must not start with `ldk-`: that whole namespace belongs to the host and its shared components, and since your CSS class prefix is derived from this id (`<pluginId>-your-class`), an `ldk-` id would land in host territory by construction and void the plugin-prefix rule (SDK check-css-namespace leg).

type.description: [Deprecated] Plugin type — no longer required. The loader infers the contribution type from declared fields such as entry/mode/themes/languages/resources. Kept only for backward compatibility. The value is an open string, not a closed enum.

core.description: Pure UI safeguard against accidental removal — marks the plugin as important, so the uninstall entry is hidden in the plugin detail UI (newcomers cannot delete it by mistake). Grants no behavioral privilege: disable/uninstall still work through the API/command layer (uninstall writes a `removed` tombstone; boot does not resurrect it). Built-in capabilities such as the settings page and marketplace come from factoryRole slots (replaceable) and are unrelated to this flag. Absent = an ordinary plugin that the UI can freely install and uninstall. Default false.

factoryRole.description: System slot role — declares which system-level feature this plugin fills. settings = settings page (opened with Ctrl+,), marketplace = plugin marketplace. Multiple plugins with the same role may legally coexist (all become slot candidates, one-to-many); the default is the first registered in stable order (core:true grants no privilege and does not claim the default), and a user-switched active candidate is persisted.

pluginRole.description: Plugin loading strategy — view = has React UI components, data = pure data (themes/languages/protocols); inferred when omitted. The value is an open string, so third parties may declare new strategy names.

appearsIn.description: Where the plugin's UI appears — declarative. Replaces iconLocation + viewRole + keepSidebarOnFocus.

iconBar.description: Icon Bar position; omitted = no icon shown

sidePanel.description: Has a Sidebar view container. Default false.

tabBar.description: Can be opened as a tab. Default false.

statusBar.description: File path of a self-drawn (code) Status Bar component, relative to the plugin root, .tsx, e.g. "src/components/statusBar.tsx" — the pool renders it from the declared URL, replacing static statusBar contributions; omit it when you only contribute static entries.

distribution.description: ⚠️ Legacy field — after the single-root flattening there is no longer any plugins/builtin vs. plugins/user distinction, so this field maps to no directory and is always normalized to user on install. Whether a plugin ships built-in is declared by `core`, not by this field. Third-party plugins should not set it.

icon.description: Icon (split of the three-image model) — plugins placed on the Icon Bar set a Type-1 monochrome silhouette glyph here (the shell Icon Bar reads only this field); for plugins not on the Icon Bar this field is the Type-2 colored identity image, which the tab bar and marketplace reuse as marketIcon ?? icon ?? default colored block. A codicon name, or a path relative to a bundled svg/png asset (inferred from the value when iconSource is omitted).

marketIcon.description: Type-2 colored plugin identity image (the earlier "cover art / scene cover" meaning is retired — embed a scene cover in the README instead) — the marketplace Sidebar row / detail header and the tab bar view label show the same image. A path relative to a bundled svg asset; omitted → falls back to icon → shared default colored block. Optional: the whole chain falls back automatically for plugins with no images, so this split is invisible to third parties.

marketIconSource.description: Identity image source — same enum as iconSource; the value is a path relative to a bundled svg asset, and when source is omitted it is inferred from the path (an explicit svg treats the path as a bare URL, which breaks already-installed plugins).

description.description: One-line description shown on the plugin detail page. Multi-line supported.

entry.description: Entry file path, relative to the plugin directory. Required for view/card/protocol.

sidebar.description: Sidebar component path; only meaningful for the view type.
sidebar.$comment: Discovered automatically by Vite glob; no plugin declaration needed

tabBehavior.description: Tab behavior declaration — the core reads this field to decide dedup / fallback / close confirmation.

isFallback.description: Automatically create this tab when no tab is open, and make it non-closable.

confirmOnClose.description: Show a confirmation dialog before closing; the value is the prompt text.

invokeBeforeClose.description: Command invoked before closing (after the confirmOnClose confirmation, before the tab closes). For example the terminal declares "close_port".

identityField.description: The single field in CreateTabOptions used to determine tab identity. Omitted = multiple instances allowed, no dedup. For example workspace declares "workspaceName" — only one tab per workspace name.

configurable.description: Declaring true → the shell auto-registers a configuration entry and injects the visible prop. The plugin author writes one line of JSON, zero code.

file.description: Single-file entry — for the theme/language types. Use either this or themes/languages.

themes.description: Array of multiple themes; only for the theme type.

languages.description: Array of multiple languages; only for the language type.

mode.description: Protocol mode. text = plain-text protocol; binary = WASM binary protocol (not available yet).

resources.description: Resource file list; only for the resource type.

requires.description: Plugin-level activation order dependency — declared by pluginId; dependencies load before this plugin. No version constraint. A missing dependency suspends the plugin (PENDING), which then loads automatically once the dependency is ready.

docs.description: Path to accompanying documentation (used with resource plugins).

i18n.description: @deprecated Use contributes.i18n instead — translation file declarations moved under contributes. Kept only for backward compatibility.

permissions.$comment: serial/filesystem/network are the first whitelist values. The value is an open string, so third parties may declare new permission names (interpreted by the main process).

iconLocation.description: Icon position in the Icon Bar. top (default, upper draggable area) or bottom (fixed bottom area).

viewRole.description: Interaction role of the view in the shell. sidebarPrimary = Sidebar first (clicking toggles the Sidebar; tabs are opened from within the Sidebar; default), tabOnly = tab-only view (opens a tab directly). tabPrimary was removed — all plugins use sidebarPrimary.

shellRendered.description: The shell renders this view itself (bypassing plugin routing). Declared only by shell-level views such as the welcome page and plugin detail page.

keepSidebarOnFocus.description: Keep the current Sidebar when this view is focused — for example the Sidebar stays unchanged while browsing the plugin detail page.

contributes.description: Contribution point declarations — mirrors VS Code package.json contributes. A core mechanism.

commands.description: Registered commands — the source consumed by the Command Palette, context menus, and keybindings.

when.description: context key when condition — e.g. activeEditor == 'terminal'

menus.description: Menu item declarations — grouped by MenuId. The built-in shell registration points are listed in the MenuRegistry MENU_SLOTS constant; MenuId is an open string, so third parties may declare any new registration point.

configuration.description: Configuration declarations — rendered automatically by the Settings Editor.

properties.description: Configuration mapping — key → { type, default, enum?, description }

uiHint.description: Settings editor rendering hint. SettingsView picks the control from the hint. An unknown hint falls back to the default rendering for its type — no error is thrown. The value is an open string, so third parties may declare new hint names.

monoOnly.description: Monospace only — meaningful only with uiHint "fontFamily". true/omitted = list monospace families only (editor fonts); false = all families (UI fonts).

minimum.description: Numeric lower bound — applies when type is number (range of the slider/numeric control)

maximum.description: Numeric upper bound — applies when type is number (range of the slider/numeric control)

step.description: Slider step — meaningful only with uiHint "slider". Defaults are derived by SettingsView from the range (0.01 for floating-point ranges).

group.description: Second-level heading within a group — keys sharing a group are rendered under a subheading on the settings page; without a group they stay flat (zero intrusion for third parties)

configurationDefaults.description: Weak defaults — suggested values this plugin gives for other configuration keys; values set by the user take precedence.

themes.description: Theme declarations — mirrors VS Code contributes.themes. Plugins contribute themes that users can switch in the theme browser / appearance settings.

label.description: Display name — e.g. My Theme Dark

uiTheme.description: Base UI theme — dark / light / high contrast

path.description: Path to the theme definition JSON file

iconThemes.description: Product icon themes — mirrors VS Code productIconThemes. Plugins declare icon sets that users can switch.

path.description: Path to the icon definition JSON file

icons.description: Shared icons — a plugin contributes icons that other plugins reference via iconSource:shared. Mirrors the VS Code icon extension point.

langDefs.description: Language definitions — mirrors VS Code contributes.languages. Declares a new language's ID/extensions/syntax highlighting/LSP support.

id.description: Language ID — e.g. cpp / python / rust

monarch.description: Optional — Monarch tokenizer definition (Monaco's built-in syntax highlighting)

command.description: Launch command — an interpreter or executable name (an interpreter such as node; a PATH binary such as clangd; or an absolute path). The python plugin uses command='node' plus args carrying the script path.

args.description: Launch arguments. Relative-path arguments resolve against the plugin root (made absolute once at registration) — e.g. 'node_modules/pyright/dist/pyright-langserver.js' → <plugin root>/node_modules/pyright/dist/pyright-langserver.js; flags such as '--stdio' are passed through verbatim. LSP binaries ship with the plugin: the SDK packaging bundles the referenced node_modules packages into the .linkdesk-plugin file (the shell no longer ships LSPs).

fileAssociations.description: File associations — file extension → plugin routing (consumed by the main-process plugin-manifest-loader). Declare only the extension plus an optional open command; this plugin's own pluginId comes from the top-level `pluginId` field (see the top-level pluginId description for the directory-name fallback).

extension.description: File extension — without the dot, e.g. dxf / stl / step

command.description: Optional — command ID to run when opening a file with this extension

displayName.description: Optional — display name in the 'Open with…' picker

languages.description: Language packs — mirrors the VS Code language extension point. A collection language pack declares multiple entries in one plugin.json.

id.description: Language code — e.g. zh / en / ja

label.description: Display name — e.g. English / Japanese / Chinese

path.description: Path to the i18n JSON translation file

titleBar.description: Title Bar button declarations — mirrors VS Code titleBar. Declares buttons on the left/right of the Title Bar: an icon button (icon) or a text-only button (label); set exactly one.

command.description: Command ID to run on click

icon.description: codicon name (e.g. codicon-settings) or image path

label.description: Button text — when set, the icon is not rendered. '$keyName' takes the value of that context key as the text (e.g. $updateButtonLabel); otherwise the value is treated as an i18n key (in this repository an i18n key is the original Chinese string).

when.description: context key when condition — the button is hidden while unmet

command.description: Command ID to run on click

icon.description: codicon name (e.g. codicon-settings) or image path

label.description: Button text — when set, the icon is not rendered. '$keyName' takes the value of that context key as the text (e.g. $updateButtonLabel); otherwise the value is treated as an i18n key (in this repository an i18n key is the original Chinese string).

when.description: context key when condition — the button is hidden while unmet

viewsContainers.description: Declares Sidebar containers — clicking this plugin's icon switches to the container. Mirrors VS Code viewsContainers.

title.description: Container title — shown in the Sidebar header

icon.description: Container icon — overrides the plugin's own icon

location.description: Container location — sidebar = Sidebar, panel = Bottom Panel, auxiliarybar = auxiliary sidebar (⚠ not wired in the shell yet: auxiliarybar containers/views are not rendered), main = Main Area tab render surface (contributed by the active factoryRole plugin via views.main[] and consumed by the shell's ShellViewRenderer when it resolves the plugin-detail tab; third-party plugins that are not marketplace-like should use sidebar/panel)

hideIfEmpty.description: Hide the container automatically when it has no active views

order.description: Sort weight within the same location. Lower values come first

mergeHeaderWhenSingle.description: Hide the view header when the container holds a single view — the title merges into the container header. Mirrors VS Code mergeViewWithContainerWhenSingleView

views.description: Register views into containers — key = container ID. Mirrors VS Code views.

id.description: Unique view ID — e.g. folders / sessions / settings

title.description: Display title — the header text of the SidebarSection. An empty string hides the collapsible header

render.description: Module path of the view component — relative to the plugin root

order.description: Sort weight within the container. Lower values on top

role.description: Container role — toolbar sticks to the top and is not overridden; section has a collapsible header and is replaced at the same level

canToggleVisibility.description: Users can toggle visibility from the Views submenu

canMoveView.description: Users can move this view to another container

minHeight.description: Declared minimum view height — the Sidebar pane PaneSash effectiveMinHeight (mirrors the VS Code view size)

hideByDefault.description: Hidden by default — users must enable it manually from the Views menu

singleViewPaneContainerTitle.description: Replaces the container title when there is a single view and the container has mergeHeaderWhenSingle

titleDescription.description: Secondary text next to the title — e.g. (5 files)

showActions.description: When actions are shown — always, whenExpanded, or default (on hover)

titleTooltip.description: Title hover tooltip — shows the full text when the title is truncated

titleActions.description: View action area declaration — the widget list on the right of the Panel tab bar / Sidebar header, carried along with the view when it moves. Three forms: icon button, dropdown menu, and split (primary button + dropdown, like the VS Code terminal's [+] New and [▾] profile list). An action is command + args; label/title are i18n keys (the original Chinese strings).

id.description: Unique widget ID — React key / dropdown open-state anchor

command.description: Command ID to run on click (split = default action of the primary button; required for icon)

icon.description: codicon class name (e.g. codicon-add) — the icon/split primary button icon

title.description: tooltip / aria-label — an i18n key (used as a text button when a split has no icon)

args.description: Command arguments — passed through as the single positional argument of executeCommand(command, args) (JSON-serializable)

label.description: Display text — an i18n key (the original Chinese string)

command.description: Command ID to run on click

args.description: Command arguments — passed through as a single positional argument

floatingPanel.description: Floating Panel declaration — declares that a view in contributes.views can be shown in a Floating Panel inside the shell. viewId must reference an already registered view: the declaration is resolved into pluginId/renderPath/title. Without it there is no 'Open in Floating Panel' context menu entry. The first declarer is settings (Ctrl+, opens the panel).

viewId.description: View ID — a view registered in contributes.views

i18n.description: Plugin-bundled translations — key = language code, value = JSON file path relative to the plugin root, e.g. { "en": "i18n/en.json" }. No zh.json is needed — Chinese keys are the built-in fallback.

menuItem.description: Menu item — aligned with the runtime ManifestMenuItem (MenuRegistry); label/order/children are recursively self-referencing. children recurses to any depth and maps one-to-one onto the runtime normalization.

command.description: Command ID (may be empty with children — a parent menu item runs no command and expands a submenu)

label.description: Display label — overrides the command title (getCommand(id).title) when present; required for a parent menu item (no command)

order.description: Sort weight — lower values come first within the same group

children.description: Nested submenus — recurses to any depth (mirrors the VS Code SubmenuAction); command may be empty when children is present

allOf.$comment: entry condition (deprecated type family) — the if clause must include required:["type"], otherwise it is vacuously true for data plugins such as theme/language that have no type (properties only validate properties that are present), which would wrongly require entry. entry is required only when type is present and matches the const.
